title: Chapter 94 — Goals, Standards, and The Self-Managed Career
intro: The goal architecture, standards as identity, and managing your career like a professional.

sections.title: Goals vs. Standards
sections.content:
A goal is something you aim for. A standard is something you refuse to fall below.

Goal: close at 45% this quarter.
Standard: I never skip discovery with any customer.

Goals change. Standards do not. The salesperson who hits goals but has no standards will eventually crash. The salesperson who maintains standards will hit goals consistently — because the standards create the habits that produce the results.

sections.title: The Self-Managed Career
sections.content:
Do not wait for your manager to develop you. Develop yourself.

Set your own goals. Track your own numbers. Identify your own weaknesses. Seek your own training. Build your own pipeline. Manage your own CRM.

The best managers will support you, coach you, and challenge you. But your career is your responsibility. The salesperson who waits for someone else to manage their growth will always be limited by their manager's time and attention.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating self-management, ask:

Does the salesperson set their own goals — or only work toward management's targets?
Do they maintain personal standards that are non-negotiable?
Are they self-aware enough to identify their own growth areas?
Do they take ownership of their career — or depend on others to develop them?
